paragraphs.text: Juang is a Munda language within the Austroasiatic family, spoken in parts of Keonjhar, Angul and Dhenkanal. It is written using Odia script. The language and its written form answer different questions: Juang names what is spoken; Odia script identifies the letters used to put it on a page.

proposed_sections.title: A house with several kinds of work

paragraphs.text: The majang, also called mandaghar, is more than a gathering place in SCSTRTI’s account. It houses musical instruments and common grain, accommodates young people and provides a place for elders’ deliberations. Music, shared resources and decisions belong to the same institution. That combination gives more substance to the term ‘community house’ than a picture of a building alone could convey.

The profile also distinguishes Thaniya, associated with the Juang Pirh homeland, from Bhagudia, associated with migration to the plains. It records an ancestral story about a Rusi couple at Rusi Tangar near Gonasika. These are ways of describing belonging and remembered origins; the story does not establish an archaeological date, and the labels need the context of the people using them.

proposed_sections.title: A language made visible in a lesson

paragraphs.text: The CIIL–NCERT Juang Primer appeared in March 2024. Its resource-person credits include teachers Kshetrabasi Juanga and Sudarsan Juanga, and community leader Nakaphudi Juanga. The named contributors matter: preparing a first reader involves choosing examples as well as arranging letters.

Its opening charts make a useful distinction. Printed page 1 presents the Juang alphabet; page 2 separately presents additional Odia letters. The pages use a shared script without treating the two languages’ teaching charts as identical.

On page 4, a rolled woven mat appears beside word labels. Pictures of a pot, maize and an axe follow below, with paired labels and progressively fainter letter forms. The learner moves between an object, a word and a shape to practise. These are details to notice in the book; the pictures alone cannot teach a newcomer the sounds.

proposed_sections.title: From a word to a sentence

paragraphs.text: The 2018 booklet places English, Odia and Juang side by side. Its contents move beyond names for objects into actions, tense and everyday sentences. Compare how a whole example is arranged across the columns, then ask a willing reader how they would say it themselves.
